newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh Islamists protest ties with India.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh Islamists protest ties with India.

text.p: An Islamic fundamentalist party in Bangladesh on Thursday urged thousands of street protesters to resist what it called the government's "unholy alliance" with mainly Hindu India.

"Let us take a vow not to bow to undue demands from India for using our land as a transit (to reach northeast Indian states) and use our sea ports," said Moulana Matiur Rahman Nizami, secretary-general of the Jamaat-e-Islami party.
He was speaking while leading thousands of party activists in a street protest in Dhaka.
The party slammed a government plan to buy electricity from India and forge a sub-regional economic cooperation bloc with India, Nepal and Bhutan, witnesses to the protest said.
"We must oppose the unholy alliance," said another Jamaat leader. The Islamists oppose the grouping, which is yet to be launched formally, because it does not include Pakistan.

Bangladesh, which broke away from Pakistan in 1971, is a member of the seven- nation South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), which also groups Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), headed by Begum Khaleda Zia, has also been critical of the Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's government for "planning to sell national interests" to India.
India helped neighbouring Bangladesh during the 1971 war against Pakistan, which the Jamaat and other orthodox Islamic groups had opposed.

Hasina, daughter of independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman who was killed in a 1975 army coup, has rejected the allegations by Jamaat and the BNP as "meaningless grumbling by distraught politicians".
